Given a normal random variable $X∼N(\mu ,{\sigma }^{2}),$ we have

$$
P(a<X<b)=P(\frac{a-\mu }{\sigma }<Z<\frac{b-\mu }{\sigma })
$$

where $Z∼N(0,1)$ is a standard normal random variable. In our case, we have $\mu =4$ and $\sigma =6.$

First, we transform $X$ into a standard normal random variable $Z$ by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-3.2<X<2.86) & =P(\frac{-3.2-4}{6}<Z<\frac{2.86-4}{6}) \\  & =P(-1.2<Z<-0.19)\end{aligned}
$$

The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14070250/assets/1ed2c43f507a4d0ddd54126bcd3efaa2fa9b56c63ea908e8567e6959e3fc67bc.png)

Now, we express the required probability in terms of $Φ(z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-1.2<Z<-0.19) & =P(Z<-0.19)-P(Z\le -1.2) \\  & =P(Z\le -0.19)-P(Z\le -1.2) \\  & =Φ(-0.19)-Φ(-1.2)\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ(-1.2) & =0.1151 \\ Φ(-0.19) & =0.4247\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-1.2<Z<-0.19) & =Φ(-0.19)-Φ(-1.2) \\  & =0.4247-0.1151 \\  & =0.3096.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we conclude that

$$
P(-3.2<X<2.86)=0.3096.
$$
